subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO & autoscaling follow-ups
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>, Samir Rao <samir@finpay.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T15:12:00Z
Subject: Post-demo: Performance SLO & autoscaling follow-ups

Hi Alex / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time to demo Redwood today. Really appreciated the clear SLO goals you shared. Per our discussion, I wanted to recap the performance/scale items and propose a few clarifying questions so we can size a deterministic plan and give you accurate cost/latency projections.

Recap of what I heard:
- Latency: target p95 end-to-end latency of ~300ms for streaming completion for inputs up to 512 tokens (lower is better).
- Throughput: baseline sustained traffic ~500 qps, with expected business-driven bursts up to ~1500 qps (bursts usually 2–5 minutes).
- Concurrency: ~100 concurrent active users at peak.
- Streaming behaviour: clients use chunked/streaming responses and want first-chunk within ~150ms.
- SLO expectations: <1% error budget for sustained operations; degradation needs graceful fallbacks.

Clarifying items we need from your side to size the autoscaling/burst config:
1) Typical request/response token distribution (avg input tokens / avg output tokens) — if you don’t have exact, a 25/75 split is fine to start.
2) For bursts, are they sudden spikes (queueing acceptable for a few seconds) or very low-latency-critical (need warm pool to avoid queueing)?
3) Any regulatory needs for warm instances (e.g., dedicated capacity vs shared with strict data isolation)?

What we propose next (simple mutual action plan):
- You send token distribution + typical QPS by endpoint (1 business day)
- We produce a config proposal that covers: reserved warm pool size, max burst pool, scale-up time targets, and expected p95 under sustained and burst loads (2 business days)
- Technical deep-dive with our infra team to validate (30–45 minutes)

Attachments: SLA_summary.pdf (high-level SLA options) and autoscaling-diagram.png (illustration of warm pool / burst flow).

Would you prefer we include a priced option for a small reserved warm pool (to guarantee <30s scale-up) vs a fully on-demand plan? I can get rough numbers in the follow-up.

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0112

From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Samir Rao <samir@finpay.com>
Date: 2026-03-01T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-demo: Performance SLO & autoscaling follow-ups

Thanks Marissa — great summary and exactly aligned with what we discussed. A few notes / answers inline: 

Token distribution: average input ~60 tokens, average output ~220 tokens (we hit some long receipts occasionally but that’s the norm).
Bursts: these are business-driven (promo blasts, batch jobs) and come up pretty quickly — we see traffic jump within 30–60s. Queueing of more than ~10s impacts UX; anything under that can be tolerated for background flows but not for interactive sessions.
Concurrency / throughput: your numbers look right for our sizing: baseline sustained ~500 qps; mid-day peaks ~900 qps; bursts up to ~1500 qps for 2–5 minutes.
Streaming: first-chunk latency is important for our UX team — under 200ms preferred.
Security: we prefer a VPC/private deployment for our production workloads, but willing to start on hosted if we can get isolated warm capacity.

Next steps from our side:
- I’ll pull per-endpoint QPS by EOD tomorrow and share a short CSV.
- We’d like a rough cost delta for a reserved warm pool that can absorb 1500 qps bursts vs fully on-demand (even a ballpark).

Also: any idea on cold-start queueing behavior? If instances scale up, will requests queue at the edge or fail fast? We need to understand request limits vs queue depth and how that maps to SLOs.

Appreciate it —
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, FinPay
alex.chen@finpay.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:30:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Post-demo: Performance SLO & autoscaling follow-ups

Dylan / Vivek — looping you both in. FinPay needs concrete answers on: warm pool sizing to hit <30s scale-up, queueing behavior and how we map queue depth to SLOs, and a priced option for reserved warm capacity vs fully on-demand.

Proposed approach:
- Offer two SKUs in the proposal: WarmPool-100 (guarantees warm instances to handle 1000 qps burst headroom) and WarmPool-200 (handles 2000 qps headroom). Both include a short SLA for scale-up time (30s / 45s).
- Technical appendix: include behavior for queueing — by default we queue up to 10s worth of requests per model group and then shed gracefully with a 429+Retry-After when necessary. For interactive flows we recommend warm pool.
- If they pick VPC private deployment, we can guarantee dedicated warm capacity (no noisy neighbors).

Action items for us:
1) Vivek: draft the tech note on queueing limits + metrics we expose (queue depth, scale events, warm pool hit rate).
2) Dylan: draft the pricing delta for WarmPool-100 and WarmPool-200 (ballpark numbers ok).
3) I’ll prepare the mutual action plan and schedule the infra deep-dive once we have their endpoint QPS CSV.

Thanks —
Marissa

Alex / Samir —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the token numbers — that helps a lot. Attached is a short mutual action plan and two preliminary priced options (ballpark) for warm capacity. High level:

Option A — WarmPool-100 (recommended starter):
- Guarantees warm instances sized to absorb ~1000 qps headroom; typical scale-up to full burst capacity in <30s for interactive flows.
- Expected p95 (streaming first-chunk): ~170–220ms under baseline and ~230–320ms during bursts (depending on model and request length).
- Ballpark delta vs on-demand: +25–35% on monthly infra cost, but reduces risk of UX regressions.

Option B — WarmPool-200 (aggressive):
- Handles ~2000 qps headroom; scale-up <45s for larger bursts.
- Expected p95: ~160–210ms baseline, ~200–280ms during bursts.
- Ballpark delta: +50–65% vs purely on-demand.

Queueing behavior: by default requests are queued briefly at the edge for up to 10s; after that we shed with clear Retry-After headers. For interactive endpoints we recommend WarmPool-100 to avoid visible queueing.

Next steps:
- Please share the per-endpoint CSV when ready.
- If this looks reasonable I’ll schedule a technical deep-dive with our infra team (Vivek suggested Thurs next week).
- If you want, we can also prepare an NDA/POC agreement; I included a DocuSign link for a standard POC SOW if you want to move quickly: https://www.docusign.com/s/ABCDEF123456

Thanks —
Marissa
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
